title: Sea otters hold hands while they sleep
text: Sea otters often hold paws while they sleep, so they don't float away from each other. A group of resting otters is called a raft.
mean: to stay on top of water
q: What's your favorite animal, and what's one cute thing it does?

title: Honey can last for thousands of years
text: Archaeologists have found pots of honey in ancient Egyptian tombs. Because honey has very little water, bacteria can't grow in it, so it almost never goes bad.
mean: becomes old and not good to eat
q: What's a food you could eat every single day?

title: Octopuses have three hearts
text: An octopus has three hearts and blue blood. Two hearts move blood to the gills, and one sends it to the rest of the body.
mean: the part of a fish or sea animal that it uses to breathe underwater
q: If you could have one animal superpower, which would you choose?

title: A forest that is one single tree
text: Pando, in Utah (USA), looks like a forest of about 47,000 trees. In fact, they all share the same roots: it's one giant living thing.
mean: the part of a plant that grows under the ground
q: Is there a special tree, park or forest in your city?

title: Bees dance to give directions
text: Honey bees do a 'waggle dance' to tell other bees where the flowers are. The direction and length of the dance show the way and the distance.
mean: how far one place is from another
q: How do you usually give directions to a friend: maps, landmarks or street names?

title: There are footprints on the Moon
text: The footprints the astronauts left on the Moon in 1969 are probably still there. There's no wind or rain on the Moon to wipe them away.
mean: marks your feet leave on the ground
q: Would you like to travel to space one day? Why or why not?

title: Penguins give pebbles as gifts
text: Some male penguins look for the perfect pebble and give it to a female penguin. If she likes it, they use it to build their nest together.
mean: a small, smooth stone
q: What's the best small gift someone has ever given you?

title: Flamingos are pink because of their food
text: Flamingos are born grey. They turn pink because of the colour in the small shrimp and algae they eat.
mean: a small sea animal you can eat
q: If you could change the colour of one thing in your life, what would it be?

title: The Eiffel Tower grows in summer
text: When it's hot, the metal of the Eiffel Tower expands, and the tower can be up to 15 centimetres taller in summer than in winter.
mean: gets bigger
q: What famous place in the world would you love to visit?

title: Elephants can 'hear' with their feet
text: Elephants can feel very low sounds through the ground with their feet. That's how they notice other elephants far away.
mean: to see, hear or feel something and pay attention to it
q: Which of your five senses do you think is the strongest?

title: You can see a full circle rainbow
text: From the ground, rainbows look like arches. From an airplane, you can sometimes see the whole thing: a complete circle.
mean: curved shapes, like the top of a door
q: What's the most beautiful thing you've seen from an airplane window?

title: Snails can sleep for three years
text: When the weather is too dry, some snails close their shell and sleep for a very long time, sometimes for years, until it rains again.
mean: the hard outside part that protects some animals
q: How many hours do you usually sleep? Is it enough?

title: Bananas are berries (but strawberries aren't)
text: For scientists, a berry has seeds inside and grows from one flower. So bananas and even avocados are berries, and strawberries are not!
mean: the small parts of a plant that grow into new plants
q: What's a fact you learned that totally surprised you?

title: Giraffes only sleep a little
text: Adult giraffes often sleep less than two hours a day, usually in short naps of a few minutes, sometimes standing up.
mean: short sleeps during the day
q: Are you a nap person? When's the best time for one?

title: Most of the ocean is still unexplored
text: Scientists have mapped only a small part of the ocean floor in detail. There are still many places, and animals, that nobody has ever seen.
mean: studied and drawn on a map
q: Would you rather explore the deep ocean or outer space?

title: Owls can turn their heads very far
text: Owls can't move their eyes, so they turn their heads instead: up to 270 degrees, almost all the way around.
mean: in place of something else
q: Are you a morning person or a night owl?

title: Hot water can freeze faster than cold water
text: Under some conditions, hot water freezes faster than cold water. It's called the Mpemba effect, and scientists still discuss why it happens.
mean: becomes ice because it's very cold
q: Do you prefer hot weather or cold weather? Why?

title: Dogs can understand many words
text: Some dogs can learn the names of more than 100 toys and bring the right one when you ask. Their brains react to the words they know.
mean: to do or feel something because of what happens
q: Do you have a pet? What's the funniest thing it does?

title: Young sunflowers follow the sun
text: Young sunflowers turn to face the sun during the day and turn back at night. When they're older, most of them stay facing east.
mean: to look towards something
q: What's your favorite flower or plant?

title: Koalas have fingerprints like ours
text: Koala fingerprints look so much like human fingerprints that it's very hard to tell them apart, even with a microscope.
mean: the lines on the ends of your fingers
q: Are there two people in your family that are hard to tell apart?

title: Music can give you chills
text: About half of people sometimes feel 'chills' when they listen to music they love. The brain releases dopamine, a happy chemical.
mean: a sudden cold feeling on your skin
q: Which song always gives you chills or good vibes?

title: Butterflies taste with their feet
text: Butterflies have taste sensors on their feet. When they land on a leaf, they 'taste' it to know if it's a good place for their eggs.
mean: to come down onto something after flying
q: What's a food you didn't like as a child but love now?

title: A cloud can weigh as much as 100 elephants
text: A normal fluffy cloud has so many tiny water drops that it can weigh around 500 tonnes, but it floats because the drops are spread out.
mean: soft and light, like cotton
q: What shapes do you see when you look at clouds?

title: Hummingbirds can fly backwards
text: Hummingbirds move their wings up to 80 times a second. They are the only birds that can fly backwards, and they can even hover in one place like a helicopter.
mean: to stay in the air in one place
q: If you could fly for one day, where would you go?

title: The oldest library in the world still works
text: The library of al-Qarawiyyin in Fez, Morocco, opened more than 1,100 years ago, and people still read and study there today.
mean: continuing until now
q: What's a book that you'd recommend to everyone?

title: Dolphins have names for each other
text: Each dolphin has its own special whistle, and other dolphins use it to call that dolphin, like a name.
mean: a high sound you make by blowing air
q: Do you have a nickname? Where does it come from?

title: Chocolate was once used as money
text: The Aztecs used cacao beans as money. You could buy food, like a tomato or an avocado, with a few beans.
mean: seeds you can eat, like coffee or cacao seeds
q: If you could pay with one food instead of money, which would it be?

title: There are more stars than grains of sand
text: Scientists think there are more stars in the universe than grains of sand on all the beaches on Earth.
mean: very small pieces of something, like sand or rice
q: When was the last time you looked at a sky full of stars?

title: Pandas spend half the day eating
text: Giant pandas eat for about 12 hours a day, mostly bamboo, because bamboo gives them very little energy.
mean: the power your body needs to move and work
q: What gives you the most energy in the morning?

title: Mount Everest grows a little every year
text: The Himalayas are still slowly rising because two pieces of the Earth push against each other. Everest grows a few millimetres a year.
mean: going up
q: Mountains, beach or city: where do you feel happiest?
